title: Care Home Support Worker - &;23p/h
description:
Residential Support Worker - Scottish Island (£23/hr, 45+ hrs/week)

Are you an experienced Residential Support Worker or Care Assistant looking for your next rewarding, high-paying contract? Take your care expertise to some of the UK's most beautiful, ruggedly scenic coastal destinations. We are fast-tracking applications for 3-month placements within established, welcoming care homes across Shetland, Orkney, and the Western Isles. Combine high earning potential with the unique experience of island living!

Note: We are looking for female staff at the moment due to requirements and demand for the role.

What We Offer
- Competitive Pay: Earn £23.00/hr (Umbrella) with guaranteed 45+ hours per week.
- Adventure & Impact: Experience breathtaking coastal landscapes and close-knit island communities.
- Relocation Support: We welcome candidates from across the UK and provide assistance with travel and placement logistics.
- Quick Start: Benefit from a streamlined hiring process.
- Contract Duration: Minimum 3 months.

Responsibilities
- Provide high-quality, person-centered care, including assistance with dressing, mobility, and personal hygiene in line with individual care plans.
- Safely administer prescribed medications and monitor resident health and overall well-being.
- Utilize safe moving and handling techniques to ensure the comfort and dignity of residents.
- Maintain a secure and supportive living environment, demonstrating the ability to manage tasks effectively, including during periods of lone working.

Qualifications
- Minimum of 1 year of professional care experience supporting older adults (care home experience preferred).
- Demonstrated competency in personal care, medication administration, and safe moving and handling practices.
- Willingness and ability to relocate or travel for a 3-month contract.
- Possession of a driving license is preferred for regional travel, though not mandatory.
- Note: Due to specific resident personal care requirements across select care homes, we have active requirements for female care professionals (Exempt under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1). We also welcome applications from all qualified care professionals for broader regional placements.

Employment Details
- Work Location: Shetland, Orkney, and the Western Isles
- Expected Hours: 45+ hours per week

Ready for Your Next Placement?

Don't wait-high-rate island placements fill quickly!

title: Night Young People Support Worker
description:
Night Young People Support Worker

We are seeking a calm and compassionate Night Support Worker to keep young people safe and supported within accommodation services in Durham.

Position: Night Young People Support Worker
Location: Durham
Salary: £26,436 per annum
Hours: Full-time, 37.5 hours per week
Contract: Permanent
Closing Date: 4 October 2026

Please note that access to transport is essential due to the location of the projects and limited public transport links.

About the Role

At Depaul UK, we believe in people's potential and take action every day to help unlock it. As a Night Young People Support Worker, you will help ensure residents within our supported accommodation remain safe, secure and well supported throughout the night.

You will respond to incidents, manage safeguarding concerns and provide practical and emotional support when residents need it. You will also help new residents settle into the service, maintain accurate records and complete essential health and safety tasks.

Working as part of a close and supportive team, your responsibilities will include:

Maintaining a safe, secure and welcoming environment overnight

Responding calmly and appropriately to incidents and emergencies

Safeguarding vulnerable young people and escalating concerns

Offering reassurance and support to residents experiencing difficulties

Helping new residents settle into the service

Conducting appropriate building, welfare and safety checks

Maintaining clear and accurate records

Communicating effectively with day staff, colleagues and external agencies

Supporting residents to develop resilience and move towards independence

About You

You may have experience within supported housing, homelessness, social care, youth work, security or another care and support environment.

You will be calm, resilient and confident working overnight, including responding to challenging or unexpected situations. You will communicate clearly, maintain professional boundaries and treat every resident with dignity and respect.

You will also be organised, dependable and able to work independently while contributing positively to a close-knit team.

About the organisation

You will be joining an established national charity providing accommodation, prevention and support services to people experiencing or at risk of homelessness.

The organisation is committed to ensuring the people it supports have a meaningful voice in how services are designed, delivered and improved.

Benefits include 26 days' annual leave, increasing with service, pension contributions of up to 7%, tailored training and development, flexible working options where suitable, a cash health plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP access and a range of retail, travel and wellbeing discounts.

Other roles you may have experience of could include Night Support Worker, Waking Night Support Worker, Youth Support Worker, Housing Support Worker, Homelessness Support Worker, Supported Housing Worker, Residential Support Worker, Project Worker or Night Concierge.

Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client - Not For Profit People.

title: Young People Support Worker
description:
Young People Support Worker

We are seeking a resilient and compassionate Support Worker to help young people overcome homelessness and move towards brighter, independent futures.

Salary: £26,436 per annum
Location: South Tyneside
Hours: 37.5 hours per week
Contract: Permanent, full time
Closing date: 1st October 2026

About the role

No two days will be the same in this rewarding role. As a Young People Support Worker, you will help young people experiencing homelessness or housing instability to build their confidence, develop practical skills and achieve greater independence.

You will manage a caseload of young people who need homelessness prevention or pre-tenancy support, developing personalised plans that help them secure accommodation and improve their wellbeing. By building trusting relationships and taking a creative approach to engagement, you will help each young person identify their strengths, overcome barriers and work towards their goals.

Your key responsibilities will include:

Managing a caseload and delivering tailored, outcome-focused support

Completing risk assessments and developing effective support plans

Providing homelessness prevention and pre-tenancy support

Delivering drop-in and planned sessions at the community hub and other local venues

Supporting young people to access education, training, employment and volunteering opportunities

Working with statutory services and partner agencies to provide coordinated support

Maintaining safeguarding, professional boundaries and accurate records

Completing health and safety checks and reporting concerns

Supporting and supervising volunteers who contribute to the service

The role will involve lone working and responding calmly and professionally to challenging situations.

About you

You will be passionate about helping young people create positive change and able to build effective relationships with individuals who may be facing significant challenges.

You will bring:

Experience of completing risk assessments and support plans

A clear understanding of safeguarding requirements and procedures

The ability to engage young people creatively and sustain positive working relationships

Confidence working independently and managing challenging situations

Good literacy, numeracy and IT skills

Strong professional boundaries and personal integrity

An effective and collaborative approach to partnership working

A flexible and responsive approach to meeting the needs of the service

A commitment to equality, diversity, dignity and respect

About Depaul UK

Depaul UK exists to end homelessness and change the lives of people affected by it. Since 1989, the charity has provided accommodation, prevention and support services to thousands of marginalised young people across the UK.

Joining Depaul UK means becoming part of an inclusive organisation where every achievement matters. You will receive tailored training and development, 26 days' annual leave rising with service, family-friendly policies, a pension with employer contributions of up to 7%, an Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP access, a cash health plan and a range of retail and lifestyle discounts.

Depaul UK welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds and is committed to fair, inclusive and safer recruitment. An appropriate DBS check will be undertaken where required.

Other roles you may have experience of could include Youth Support Worker, Homelessness Support Worker, Housing Support Worker, Key Worker, Project Worker, Tenancy Support Worker, Community Support Worker or Young Person's Support Worker.

Please note this role is advertised by NFP People, the recruitment agency acting on behalf of Depaul UK.
